subject: Search trimmedsequence duplication in genome reference (fasta file) using gl.blast()

messages.author: e128ae1057d75fd3
messages.subject: Search trimmedsequence duplication in genome reference (fasta file) using gl.blast()
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to use the gl.blast() function to search for identical sequences between trimmedsequence and the reference genome/sequence with the default setting of 70% identity. I noticed that the BLAST results only return the most identical sequence (top 1) from the reference genome/sequence.

Is there an option to search for duplicated sequences (paralogs?) in the reference genome/sequence and display multiple BLAST results as a list?

I would greatly appreciate any assistance with this. Thank you.

Regards,

Rizki

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Search trimmedsequence duplication in genome reference (fasta file) using gl.blast()
parts:
Hi Rizki,

Those intermediary files can be recovered from the temporal directory (tempdir) as shown in the code below:

Cheers,
Luis 

library(dartRverse)
t1 <- platypus.gl
# assigning chromosome
t1$chromosome <- t1$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# assigning SNP position
t1$position <- t1$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# running blast
t2 <- gl.blast(t1,
               ref_genome = "X4.fasta")
blast_files <- list.files(path = tempdir(),
           pattern = "Blast",
           full.names = TRUE
           )
# [1] "Blast_filtered_1038c4bc2326b"   "Blast_one_hit_1038c3a7c35a8"    "Blast_unfiltered_1038c2a47bce4"
# filtered aligned sequences
Blast_filtered  <- readRDS(blast_files[1])
# one hit per sequence
Blast_one_hit <- readRDS(blast_files[2])
# unfiltered aligned sequences
Blast_unfiltered <- readRDS(blast_files[3])
